subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which famous overland route carried migrants by wagon train to the Pacific Northwest?
questions.explain: The Oregon Trail was the main wagon route to the Pacific Northwest.

questions.q: The near-extermination of which animal devastated the Plains Indians' way of life?
questions.explain: The destruction of the buffalo herds undermined the Plains Indians' survival.

questions.q: Which 1851 treaty first tried to set boundaries for Plains tribes and protect trail traffic?
questions.explain: The 1851 Fort Laramie Treaty attempted to define tribal lands and protect the trails.

questions.q: In which year did the California Gold Rush draw thousands of '49ers' westward?
questions.explain: The Gold Rush began in 1848-49, giving the prospectors the name '49ers'.

questions.q: Which 1830 law forced many Native American nations to move west of the Mississippi River?
questions.explain: The 1830 Indian Removal Act forced eastern tribes onto the 'Trail of Tears' westward.

questions.q: Which religious group migrated to the Salt Lake valley in Utah under Brigham Young?
questions.explain: The Mormons, led by Brigham Young, settled around the Great Salt Lake from 1847.

questions.q: Which group of Mormon pioneers reached the Salt Lake valley in 1847 under Brigham Young?
questions.explain: The Mormons (Latter-day Saints) settled the Salt Lake valley from 1847 to escape persecution.

questions.q: Discovery of gold in which hills in 1874 broke a treaty and provoked the Sioux wars?
questions.explain: Gold found in the sacred Black Hills in 1874 sparked conflict leading to the Little Bighorn.

questions.q: The long drive of cattle from Texas to railheads such as Abilene is most associated with which figures?
questions.explain: Cattle drives north created the cowboy culture and cattle ranching industry.

questions.q: Which 1864 attack saw Colorado militia massacre a peaceful Cheyenne and Arapaho camp?
questions.explain: The Sand Creek Massacre of 1864 killed mostly women and children in a Cheyenne camp.

questions.q: Which Sioux war leader, alongside Crazy Horse, defeated Custer at the Little Bighorn?
questions.explain: Sitting Bull was a Sioux leader at the 1876 Battle of the Little Bighorn.

questions.q: The 1862 Homestead Act offered settlers how much free land if they farmed it for five years?
questions.explain: The Homestead Act granted 160 acres to settlers who farmed it for five years.

questions.q: What name was given to the cowboys' long journeys herding cattle north to railroad towns?
questions.explain: Cattle drives took Texas longhorns north to railheads such as Abilene and Dodge City.

questions.q: What name was given to settlers who claimed and farmed free land under the 1862 Act?
questions.explain: Settlers who claimed and farmed free land under the Homestead Act were called homesteaders.

questions.q: The religious dance that alarmed the US Army and preceded the 1890 Wounded Knee massacre was called the what?
questions.explain: The Ghost Dance movement spread among the Sioux and alarmed authorities before Wounded Knee in 1890.

questions.q: The 1849 California Gold Rush followed the discovery of gold at which location in 1848?
questions.explain: Gold was found at Sutter's Mill in 1848, triggering the 1849 rush of the '49ers'.

questions.q: In which year did the United States acquire huge western territory through the Louisiana Purchase, opening the West?
questions.explain: The 1803 Louisiana Purchase from France roughly doubled US territory and spurred westward expansion.

questions.q: At which 1876 battle were Custer and his men of the 7th Cavalry wiped out?
questions.explain: Custer was killed at the Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876.

questions.q: The 1890 massacre that effectively ended Native American armed resistance occurred at which site?
questions.explain: The Wounded Knee Massacre of 1890 marked the end of the Plains Wars.

questions.q: Completion of which 1869 project linked the east and west coasts of the USA?
questions.explain: The first Transcontinental Railroad was completed in 1869 at Promontory Summit.

questions.q: Which cheap fencing technology helped homesteaders enclose land on the open Plains?
questions.explain: Cheap barbed wire let homesteaders fence land and protect crops from cattle on the Plains.

questions.q: The belief that the USA was destined to expand across the continent was called what?
questions.explain: 'Manifest Destiny' justified American westward expansion to the Pacific.
